questions.question: Question 1: How often do you ride the bus? Why do you ride it?
questions.reference_answer: I ride the bus about three or four times a week. I ride it because it is convenient and cheaper than taking a taxi, and it can drop me off close to my office.
questions.keywords: question how often do you ride the bus why do you ride

questions.question: Question 2: What are some reasons for choosing to ride the bus, such as punctual arrival, friendly service, or low cost? Which one would you choose, and why?
questions.reference_answer: There are several reasons why people choose to ride the bus. For example, the bus usually arrives on time, the drivers and staff provide friendly service, and the fare is much lower than other transportation. If I had to choose, I would pick punctual arrival. In my daily commute, arriving on time is the most important, because I need to reach the office before the morning meeting. No matter how cheap or comfortable the bus is, being late would cause a lot of stress.
questions.keywords: question what are some reasons for choosing to ride the bus such

questions.question: Question 3: Do you think the bus service in your city will become more popular or less popular in the future? Why?
questions.reference_answer: I think the bus service in my city will become more popular in the future. First, as traffic congestion gets worse, more people will look for alternatives to driving. Taking the bus allows commuters to avoid the stress of finding parking and dealing with rush-hour traffic. Second, with growing concerns about the environment, many people are trying to reduce their carbon footprint. Buses are a more eco-friendly option compared to private cars, since one bus can carry dozens of passengers at once. Finally, the city government has been investing in new bus lanes and upgrading the fleet to electric buses, which will make the service faster, quieter, and more comfortable. All of these factors will likely attract more riders in the coming years.

questions.question: Do you think people in the past spent more time reading than people do now? Why or why not?
questions.reference_answer: I believe people in the past did spend more time reading than people do today. The first reason is that there were fewer entertainment options in the past. Before smartphones and streaming services, people had limited ways to kill time, so reading books and newspapers was one of the most common activities. As a result, reading became a daily habit for many people. The second reason is that reading was more closely connected to work and study. In the past, people had to read manuals, letters, and long reports carefully to finish their jobs, which naturally took up a large part of their day. Today, however, information comes in the form of short videos, quick messages, and audio content, so people tend to consume knowledge faster and read fewer long texts. Finally, many young people today feel that scrolling through their phones is more relaxing than reading, which further reduces the time they spend with books. In short, because of richer entertainment and faster ways of getting information, I think people today read less than people in the past.
questions.topic: 过去与现在的阅读习惯
